sections.readable_text: Which expression gives all of the zeros of the function [MATH: f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right)?]

sections.normalized_html:
The zeros of [MATH: y=\cot x] are given by

[MATH: x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi,] where [MATH: n] is an integer.

To find the zeros of [MATH: f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right),] we replace the [MATH: x] on the left-hand side of the above with [MATH: \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right).] This gives

[MATH: 2x + \dfrac \pi 6 = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi.]

Solving for [MATH: x,] we get

[MATH: 2x + (π)/(6)|= (π)/(2) + nπ; 2x|= (π)/(2) + nπ − (π)/(6); 2x|= (π)/(3) + nπ; x|= (π)/(6) + (nπ)/(2).]

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are [MATH: x = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{n\pi}{2},] where [MATH: n] is an integer.
